conclusion: Migration, security hardening, persistence recovery, deployment safeguards, tests, packaging, and documentation passed release review. Independent code review found no remaining P0/P1 after the subscription-stream denial-of-service fix.
verifiedFixes: CLI and MCP share the in-process ComfyUI client; the legacy duplicate client was removed
workflow, asset, job, and output resources are addressable and output resources can be reused without download/re-upload
server, node, and model discovery is paginated, deterministic, and URL-encodes path segments
network calls use explicit connect/read or execution deadlines
running job cancellation is rejected instead of using ComfyUI global interrupt
static bearer tokens map to stable principal_id owners across rotation and reject malformed token, principal, and scope configurations
request IDs and bearer headers are bounded and validated
ordinary HTTP requests and long-lived subscriptions/listen streams use separate fail-fast concurrency pools with per-principal subscription quotas
subscription scanning is offloaded from the event loop and SDK subscription capacity is bounded
retention cleanup uses bounded lock batches and does not delete assets referenced by non-terminal jobs
management mutations use durable intent/success/failure audit records, operation fingerprints, audit-only recovery, and no-reexecution retry semantics
structured logs, process metrics, maintenance pruning, multi-worker guardrails, pinned Actions, Dependabot, lockfile, build, install, and Trusted Publishing release workflows are present
